claim: Under chronic or severe liver injury, liver progenitor cells (LPCs) of biliary origin expand and contribute to the regeneration of hepatocytes and cholangiocytes.
source: Under chronic or severe liver injury, liver progenitor cells (LPCs) of biliary origin are known to expand and contribute to the regeneration of hepatocytes and cholangiocytes.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field, supported by the context of the manuscript.

claim: The regeneration process involving LPCs is called ductular reaction (DR), which is accompanied by dynamic remodeling of biliary tissue.
source: This regeneration process is called ductular reaction (DR), which is accompanied by dynamic remodeling of biliary tissue.
evidence: This is a definitional statement based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Lutheran (Lu)/Basal cell adhesion molecule (BCAM) regulates the morphogenesis of DR depending on liver disease models.
source: Here, we show that Lutheran (Lu)/Basal cell adhesion molecule (BCAM) regulates the morphogenesis of DR depending on liver disease models.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Lu+ and Lu- biliary cells isolated from injured liver exhibit opposite phenotypes in cell motility and duct formation capacities in vitro.
source: Lu+ and Lu- biliary cells isolated from injured liver exhibit opposite phenotypes in cell motility and duct formation capacities in vitro.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from scratch assays and cyst formation assays shown in Figure 3.

claim: By overexpression of Lu, Lu- biliary cells acquire the phenotype of Lu+ biliary cells.
source: By overexpression of Lu, Lu- biliary cells acquire the phenotype of Lu+ biliary cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from retroviral overexpression experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: Lu-deficient mice showed severe defects in DR.
source: Lu-deficient mice showed severe defects in DR.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Bcam knockout mice shown in Figure 6.

claim: In acutely injured or surgically resected livers, regeneration is usually achieved by proliferation and hypertrophy of residual hepatocytes.
source: In acutely injured or surgically resected livers, regeneration is usually achieved by proliferation and hypertrophy of residual hepatocytes (Fausto and Campbell, 2003; Miyaoka et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Under chronic or severe liver injury that impairs the proliferation of hepatocytes, liver progenitor cell (LPC) has been postulated to contribute to liver regeneration by differentiating into hepatocytes and biliary epithelial cells.
source: By contrast, under chronic or severe liver injury that impairs the proliferation of hepatocytes, liver progenitor cell (LPC) has been postulated to contribute to liver regeneration by differentiating into hepatocytes and biliary epithelial cells (BECs), also known as cholangiocytes (Thorgeirsson, 1996; Fausto, 2004; Miyajima et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: DRs are frequently observed in human chronic liver diseases and rodent models including fatty liver disease and cholangiopathy.
source: DRs are frequently observed in human chronic liver diseases and rodent models including fatty liver disease and cholangiopathy (Shafritz and Dabeva, 2002; Roskams et al., 2003; Gouw et al., 2011; Wood et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In zebrafish models, biliary cells have been reported to contribute to regenerating hepatocytes after substantial loss of hepatocytes.
source: In zebrafish models, biliary cells have been reported to contribute to regenerating hepatocytes after substantial loss of hepatocytes (Choi et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In mouse models, accumulating evidence by in vitro assay or transplantation experiments of biliary cells supports the presence of potential LPC with clonogenicity and bi-lineage differentiation capacity in the biliary compartment.
source: In mouse models, accumulating evidence by in vitro assay or transplantation experiments of biliary cells supports the presence of potential LPC with clonogenicity and bi-lineage differentiation capacity in the biliary compartment (Suzuki et al., 2008a; Okabe et al., 2009; Dorrell et al., 2011; Lu et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: A recent study using in vivo genetic lineage tracing experiment demonstrated that biliary cells can regenerate hepatocytes as facultative LPC under impaired hepatocyte regeneration in mice.
source: In addition, a recent study using in vivo genetic lineage tracing experiment demonstrated that biliary cells can regenerate hepatocytes as facultative LPC under impaired hepatocyte regeneration in mice (Raven et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Genetically manipulated mice with defects in DR have been reported to show impaired recovery from chronic liver injury.
source: In fact, genetically manipulated mice with defects in DR have been reported to show impaired recovery from chronic liver injury (Ishikawa et al., 2012; Takase et al., 2013; Shin et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Two dietary models using 3,5-Diethoxycarbonyl-1,4-dihydrocollidine supplemented (DDC) diet and choline-deficient, ethionine-supplemented (CDE) diet have been extensively utilized to characterize LPC in mice.
source: In particular, two dietary models using 3,5-Diethoxycarbonyl-1,4-dihydrocollidine supplemented (DDC) diet and choline-deficient, ethionine-supplemented (CDE) diet have been extensively utilized to characterize LPC in mice for many years (Preisegger et al., 1999; Akhurst et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Both CDE and DDC models induce massive DR, but the pathological features resulting from these two methods are quite distinct.
source: Although both models induce massive DR, the pathological features resulting from these two methods are quite distinct
evidence: This is supported by the subsequent description and citations in the text.

claim: CDE-induced injury is thought to be a mouse model of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease with extensive hepatic damage.
source: CDE-induced injury is thought to be a mouse model of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease with extensive hepatic damage (Knight et al., 2005; Aharoni-Simon et al., 2011)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: DDC-induced injury is considered as a model of chronic cholangiopathy with portal biliary damage and severe cholestasis.
source: while DDC-induced injury is considered as a model of chronic cholangiopathy with portal biliary damage and severe cholestasis (Fickert et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Morphological and functional heterogeneity of ductal cells is evident in DRs originating from many different pathological conditions in human patients and rodent models.
source: In fact, it has been reported that morphological and functional heterogeneity of ductal cells is evident in DRs originating from many different pathological conditions in human patients and rodent models (Sell, 1998; Alvaro et al., 2007; Priester et al., 2010; Kaneko et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: CDE-induced DR extends outwards away from the portal vein, showing primitive ductules with spindle-like shape.
source: CDE- and DDC-induced DR exhibited quite distinct morphology; the former extends outwards away from the portal vein, showing primitive ductules with spindle-like shape
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: DDC-induced DR remains around the portal vein, forming obvious bile duct-like structures.
source: while the latter remains around the portal vein, forming obvious bile duct-like structures.
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Lu, also known as Basal Cell Adhesion Molecule (BCAM) or CD239, is a member of the immunoglobulin superfamily.
source: Lu, also known as Basal Cell Adhesion Molecule (BCAM) or CD239 is a member of the immunoglobulin superfamily, which is composed of five Ig-like domains on the extracellular site, a single transmembrane domain and a short C-terminal cytoplasmic tail (Parsons et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Lu is composed of five Ig-like domains on the extracellular site, a single transmembrane domain and a short C-terminal cytoplasmic tail.
source: Lu, also known as Basal Cell Adhesion Molecule (BCAM) or CD239 is a member of the immunoglobulin superfamily, which is composed of five Ig-like domains on the extracellular site, a single transmembrane domain and a short C-terminal cytoplasmic tail (Parsons et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Lu is known as a laminin receptor, which has been studied in context of sickle cell disease.
source: Lu is known as a laminin receptor, which has been studied in context of sickle cell disease (Udani et al., 1998; El Nemer et al., 1999)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Lu is capable of binding to laminin-511/521 via laminin alpha5 (Lama5) chain.
source: and is capable of binding to laminin-511/521 via laminin alpha5 (Lama5) chain (Parsons et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Lu/BCAM is widely expressed in cells and tissues including hematopoietic cells, placenta and kidney.
source: It has been reported that Lu/BCAM is widely expressed in cells and tissues including hematopoietic cells, placenta and kidney, and is developmentally regulated in human liver (Parsons et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Lu/BCAM is developmentally regulated in human liver.
source: It has been reported that Lu/BCAM is widely expressed in cells and tissues including hematopoietic cells, placenta and kidney, and is developmentally regulated in human liver (Parsons et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Both protocols of feeding CDE and DDC diet for 3 weeks induced robust DR accompanied by biliary cell expansion.
source: Both protocols of feeding CDE and DDC diet for 3 weeks induced robust DR accompanied by biliary cell expansion.
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: CDE-induced biliary cells displayed primitive capillary-like morphology, invading into the parenchymal area extensively.
source: CDE-induced biliary cells displayed primitive capillary-like morphology, invading into the parenchymal area extensively
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: DDC-induced biliary cells exhibited remarkable duct-like structure, remaining around the periportal area.
source: while DDC-induced biliary cells exhibited remarkable duct-like structure, remaining around the periportal area (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Lu was detected in extending biliary cells of the CDE-fed liver.
source: Co-staining of liver sections using anti-EpCAM and anti-Lu antibodies revealed that Lu was detected in extending biliary cells of the CDE-fed liver
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Lu signals could not be found in biliary cells of DDC-fed liver except intense signal in EpCAM- ducts.
source: whereas we could not find such signals in biliary cells of DDC-fed liver except intense signal in EpCAM- ducts (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Lu is stained in hepatic arteries and portal vein of adult human liver.
source: As reported by the previous paper that Lu is stained in hepatic arteries and portal vein of adult human liver (Parsons et al., 1995)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The EpCAM- duct with strong Lu fluorescence in DDC-fed liver is hepatic artery.
source: co-staining of Lu and platelet endothelial cell adhesion molecule (PECAM), an endothelial marker, in the DDC-fed liver revealed that the EpCAM- duct with strong fluorescence is hepatic artery (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: In untreated normal liver, most EpCAM+ biliary cells showed moderate expression of Lu.
source: In untreated normal liver, FCM and immunohistochemical analyses demonstrated that most EpCAM+ biliary cells showed moderate expression of Lu (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by flow cytometric and immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Approximately 35% of EpCAM+ cells in CDE-fed liver showed high expression of Lu.
source: By contrast, approximately 35% of EpCAM+ cells in CDE-fed liver showed high expression of Lu
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by flow cytometric data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Nearly half of EpCAM+ cells in DDC-fed liver exhibited low or negative expression of Lu.
source: whereas nearly half of EpCAM+ cells in DDC-fed liver exhibited low or negative expression of Lu (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by flow cytometric data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Lu+ BC displayed spindle-like shape while Lu- BC showed epithelial-like morphology even after several passages.
source: Interestingly, similar to the morphological characteristics of DR in vivo, Lu+ BC displayed spindle-like shape while Lu- BC showed epithelial-like morphology even after several passages (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by microscopic data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Actin fibers and pseudopods are formed in the atypical cell body of Lu+ BC.
source: Fluorescent staining using Phalloidin demonstrated that the actin fibers and pseudopods are formed in the atypical cell body of Lu+ BC
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunocytochemical data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: F-actin accumulates in the periphery of round-shaped cell body of Lu- BC.
source: while F-actin accumulates in the periphery of round-shaped cell body of Lu- BC (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunocytochemical data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The expression profile of Lu was maintained in cultured Lu+ BC and Lu- BC.
source: Furthermore, FCM analysis of cultured Lu+ BC and Lu- BC revealed that the expression profile of Lu was maintained in each cell; Luhigh-derived biliary cells continued to express Lu at a high level, while Lu-/low-derived biliary cells hardly expressed Lu (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by flow cytometric data shown in Figure 2D (referred to as 2C in the text).

claim: Several stem cell markers such as CD24 and CD44 were expressed similarly between Lu+ BC and Lu- BC.
source: By contrast, several stem cell markers such as CD24 and CD44 were expressed similarly between Lu+ BC and Lu- BC
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by flow cytometric data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Lu+ BC showed significantly higher motility capacity than Lu- BC.
source: As expected, Lu+ BC showed significantly higher motility capacity than Lu- BC (Figure 3A)
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by scratch assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Lu- BC formed a large number of cystic structures after 6 days of 3D culture.
source: After 6 days of culture, Lu- BC formed a large number of cystic structures
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by 3D culture data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Lu+ BC formed only small cell aggregates after 6 days of 3D culture.
source: while Lu+ BC formed only small cell aggregates, demonstrating that Lu- BC has higher duct-forming capacity than Lu+ BC (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by 3D culture data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Lu- BC has higher duct-forming capacity than Lu+ BC.
source: demonstrating that Lu- BC has higher duct-forming capacity than Lu+ BC (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the 3D culture data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: mLu-transduced Lu- BC (Lu- BC-mLu) showed morphological change into a spindle-like shape.
source: The mLu-transduced Lu- BC (Lu- BC-mLu) showed morphological change into a spindle-like shape
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by microscopic data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: GFP-transduced control Lu- BC (Lu- BC-GFP) retained a round shape.
source: while GFP-transduced control (Lu- BC-GFP) retained a round shape (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by microscopic data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Lu- BC-mLu showed higher mobility than Lu- BC-GFP in the scratch assay.
source: In the scratch assay, Lu- BC-mLu showed higher mobility than Lu- BC-GFP (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by scratch assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Lu- BC-mLu showed reduced cyst-forming capacity, resulting in the formation of numerous small aggregates.
source: In contrast, the cyst formation assay demonstrated the reduced cyst-forming capacity of Lu- BC-mLu, resulting in the formation of numerous small aggregates (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by 3D culture data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Most expanding biliary cells are fully surrounded by Lama5 in both CDE- and DDC-injured livers.
source: Intriguingly, double staining of EpCAM and Lama5 revealed that most expanding biliary cells are fully surrounded by Lama5 in both liver injury models (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The expression of Lama5 mRNA was verified in both EpCAM+ biliary cells isolated from CDE- and DDC-injured livers.
source: Indeed, the expression of Lama5 mRNA was verified in both EpCAM+ biliary cells isolated from CDE- and DDC-injured livers (Figure 5B)
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Lu binds to Lama5 competitively with Integrinα3β1/α6β1 and promotes tumor cell migration by modulating Integrin-mediated cell attachment to Laminin-511 protein.
source: It has been reported that Lu binds to Lama5 competitively with Integrinα3β1/α6β1 and promotes tumor cell migration by modulating Integrin-mediated cell attachment to Laminin-511 protein (Kikkawa et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: All integrin components (Itga3, Itga6, Itgb1) were expressed in Lu- BC and Lu+ BC.
source: As shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2, all integrin components were expressed in Lu- BC and Lu+ BC
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The inhibition of Itgb1 signaling did not affect the expression of Lu in Lu- BC.
source: Although the inhibition of Itgb1 signaling did not affect the expression of Lu (Figure 5—figure supplement 3)
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Inhibition of Itgb1 signaling dramatically changed Lu- BC to Lu+ BC-like phenotype in both scratch assay and cyst formation assay.
source: it dramatically changed Lu- BC to Lu+ BC-like phenotype in both scratch assay and cyst formation assay (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Lu+ BC acquired cyst formation capacity by the activation of Itgb1.
source: As a result, Lu+ BC acquired cyst formation capacity by the activation of Itgb1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: Bcam KO mice were healthy, showing no obvious developmental abnormality.
source: The Bcam KO mice were healthy, showing no obvious developmental abnormality as reported previously (Rahuel et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, also supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The proliferation of biliary cells occurred in both WT and Bcam KO mouse livers when mice were fed the CDE diet.
source: When mice were fed the CDE diet, the proliferation of biliary cells occurred in both WT and Bcam KO mouse livers (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Lu-deficient biliary cells failed to spread outwards from the portal vein while WT biliary cells extended into the parenchymal area in CDE-fed mice.
source: To our surprise, Lu-deficient biliary cells failed to spread outwards from the portal vein while WT biliary cells extended into the parenchymal area.
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The migrating distance of biliary cells from the portal vein was significantly shorter in Bcam KO mice than WT mice in the CDE model.
source: The migrating distance of biliary cells from the portal vein was significantly shorter in Bcam KO mice than WT mice (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: In the DDC model, the migrating distance of biliary cells from the portal vein showed no significant difference between WT and Bcam KO mice.
source: By contrast, in the DDC model, the migrating distance of biliary cells from the portal vein showed no significant difference between WT and Bcam KO mice (Figure 6D and E).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6D and E.

claim: A slight hyperplasia of duct-like structures was observed in Bcam KO mice in both DDC and CDE models.
source: However, a slight hyperplasia of duct-like structures was observed in Bcam KO mice in both DDC and CDE models (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Freshly isolated EpCAM+ biliary cells from WT CDE-fed mouse livers showed spindle-like shape and pseudopods on the dish.
source: Moreover, freshly isolated EpCAM+ biliary cells from WT CDE-fed mouse livers showed spindle-like shape and pseudopods on the dish
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by microscopic data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Freshly isolated EpCAM+ biliary cells from Bcam KO CDE-fed mice predominantly exhibited rounder morphology resembling Lu- BC.
source: while those from Bcam KO mice predominantly exhibited rounder morphology resembling Lu- BC (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by microscopic data shown in Figure 6G.

claim: CD239 was stained in DR in patients of chronic liver disease including non-alcoholic steatohepatitis, hepatitis B virus and hepatitis C virus.
source: Intriguingly, CD239 was stained in DR in patients of chronic liver disease including non-alcoholic steatohepatitis, hepatitis B virus and hepatitis C virus (Figure 7)
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The expression profile of Lu is conserved in humans.
source: suggesting that the expression profile of Lu is conserved in humans.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of CD239 staining in human liver disease samples.

claim: DDC-injury is a model of chronic cholangiopathy, which requires replenishment of cholangiocytes or bile ducts to be recovered.
source: This is reasonable because DDC-injury is a model of chronic cholangiopathy, which requires replenishment of cholangiocytes or bile ducts to be recovered.
evidence: This is an inference based on the nature of the DDC model and previous knowledge.

claim: Mice with impaired DR causes severe jaundice in the DDC model.
source: In fact, it has been reported that mice with impaired DR causes severe jaundice in the DDC model (Takase et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The downregulation of Lu in LPC may represent a process of cholangiocytic differentiation and reinforcement of duct formation for bile excretion in the DDC model.
source: Therefore, the downregulation of Lu in LPC may represent a process of cholangiocytic differentiation and reinforcement of duct formation for bile excretion in the DDC model.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: The contribution of LPC derived from biliary component to hepatocyte regeneration has been reported in the CDE model using two different lineage tracing approaches based on BEC marker genes, Osteopontin (Spp1) and Hnf1β.
source: The contribution of LPC derived from biliary component to hepatocyte regeneration has been reported in the CDE model using two different lineage tracing approaches based on BEC marker genes, Osteopontin (Spp1) and Hnf1β (Español-Suñer et al., 2012; Rodrigo-Torres et al., 2014)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The valid but low contribution of LPC of biliary origin to hepatocytic differentiation may be explained by robust proliferation of mature hepatocytes.
source: The valid but low contribution of LPC of biliary origin to hepatocytic differentiation may be explained by robust proliferation of mature hepatocytes, because hepatocyte-mediated regeneration is not inhibited in the CDE model.
evidence: This is an inference based on the characteristics of the CDE model.

claim: A combination of CDE-injury and inhibition of hepatocyte proliferation causes physiologically significant and higher contribution of biliary cells to hepatic regeneration.
source: This notion is strongly supported by a more recent report from Forbes's group suggesting that a combination of CDE-injury and inhibition of hepatocyte proliferation causes physiologically significant and higher contribution of biliary cells to hepatic regeneration (Raven et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Lu-mediated high motility of LPC in the CDE model may contribute to the rapid delivery of hepatic progenitor cells to the damaged parenchymal area far from the portal vein.
source: Therefore, Lu-mediated high motility of LPC in the CDE model may contribute to the rapid delivery of hepatic progenitor cells to the damaged parenchymal area far from the portal vein.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: Several immune cell-derived cytokines such as TNF-related WEAK inducer of apoptosis (TWEAK), interleukin-6 and interleukin-22 have been shown to be pro-mitotic for LPCs.
source: Several immune cell-derived cytokines such as TNF-related WEAK inducer of apoptosis (TWEAK), interleukin-6 and interleukin-22 have been shown to be pro-mitotic for LPCs (Jakubowski et al., 2005; Yeoh et al., 2007; Feng et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Cell signaling pathways including Wnt, Notch, HGF and EGF are reportedly responsible for fate decisions of LPCs.
source: Cell signaling pathways including Wnt, Notch, HGF and EGF are reportedly responsible for fate decisions of LPCs (Boulter et al., 2012; Fiorotto et al., 2013; Kitade et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The escape of LPCs from the laminin basement favors their hepatocytic differentiation.
source: It has been reported that the escape of LPCs from the laminin basement favors their hepatocytic differentiation (Español-Suñer et al., 2012; Paku et al., 2004)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Laminin aids maintenance of LPC and biliary cell phenotype.
source: while laminin aids maintenance of LPC and biliary cell phenotype (Lorenzini et al., 2010; Boulter et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Lama5 KO mice show defects in bile duct formation during liver development.
source: Consistently, it has been reported that Lama5 KO mice show defects in bile duct formation during liver development and that Itgb1 signaling is required for cholangiocytic differentiation from hepatoblast, a fetal-type LPC (Tanimizu et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Itgb1 signaling is required for cholangiocytic differentiation from hepatoblast, a fetal-type LPC.
source: Consistently, it has been reported that Lama5 KO mice show defects in bile duct formation during liver development and that Itgb1 signaling is required for cholangiocytic differentiation from hepatoblast, a fetal-type LPC (Tanimizu et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Itgb1 signaling in the context of laminin/integrin axis is crucial for biliary regeneration and duct formation from LPC.
source: It is therefore highly probable that Itgb1 signaling in the context of laminin/integrin axis is crucial for biliary regeneration and duct formation from LPC.
evidence: This is an inference based on previous literature and the study's findings.

claim: Prolonged Kupffer cell (KC) depletion did not influence the proliferation of LPCs but reduced their invasive behavior in the CDE model.
source: Intriguingly, Hul et al. reported that prolonged Kupffer cell (KC) depletion did not influence the proliferation of LPCs but reduced their invasive behavior in the CDE model (Van Hul et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The LPCs of KC-depleted mice exhibit phenotype resembling cells of biliary lineage with rounder morphology.
source: The LPCs of KC-depleted mice exhibit phenotype resembling cells of biliary lineage with rounder morphology.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature (Van Hul et al., 2011).

claim: The LPCs in KC-depleted mice remain closer to the portal area, in places delineating a pseudo-lumen.
source: More interestingly, the LPCs remain closer to the portal area, in places delineating a pseudo-lumen.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature (Van Hul et al., 2011).

claim: The phenotypic change of LPCs by KC depletion closely resembles that of Bcam KO mice in the CDE diet.
source: This phenotypic change of LPCs by KC depletion closely resembles that of Bcam KO mice in the CDE diet.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by comparing the findings from the study with previous literature.

claim: Hepatic macrophage played a role in promoting LPC specification to hepatocytes by expressing Wnt3a in the CDE model.
source: On the other hand, Boulter et al. reported that hepatic macrophage played a role in promoting LPC specification to hepatocytes by expressing Wnt3a in the CDE model (Boulter et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Hepatic macrophages may be a key regulator of Lu expression in a process of LPC specification.
source: These evidences suggest that hepatic macrophages may be a key regulator of Lu expression in a process of LPC specification.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on previous literature.

claim: The expression profile of Lu in biliary cells dramatically changes during DR depending on the type of liver injury, which in turn dictates the morphological characteristics of biliary cells such as cell motility and duct formation.
source: In conclusion, the present study demonstrates that the expression profile of Lu in biliary cells dramatically changes during DR depending on the type of liver injury, which in turn dictates the morphological characteristics of biliary cells such as cell motility and duct formation (Figure 8).
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by all the experimental data presented.

claim: Lu is a novel marker for classification of DR.
source: Thus, Lu is a novel marker for classification of DR and an interesting functional molecule for investigating the nature of LPCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: Lu is an interesting functional molecule for investigating the nature of LPCs.
source: Thus, Lu is a novel marker for classification of DR and an interesting functional molecule for investigating the nature of LPCs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: EpCAM has been previously identified as a marker for murine LPC/BEC.
source: We have previously identified Epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM) as a marker for murine LPC/BEC (Okabe et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Immunostaining of CK19 showed a pattern similar to that of EpCAM in CDE- and DDC-induced DR.
source: Similarly, immunostaining of CK19, another LPC marker, showed a pattern similar to that of EpCAM (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Lu was identified as a marker for hepatoblasts, a fetal type LPC during liver development.
source: we have identified Lu as a marker for hepatoblasts, a fetal type LPC during liver development.
evidence: This is mentioned as previous work by the authors, though not explicitly cited.

claim: LPCs are able to form cyst-like luminal structures with biliary epithelial polarity in a three-dimensional (3D) organoid culture.
source: As previously reported, LPCs are able to form cyst-like luminal structures with biliary epithelial polarity in a three-dimensional (3D) organoid culture (Tanimizu et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Lu is capable of binding to Laminin-511 and -521.
source: Because Lu is known to be a receptor for Lama5 and bind to Laminin-511 and -521
evidence: This is established knowledge about Lu, supported by previous literature.

claim: Laminins (Laminin-511/521) are ligands for Integrinα3β1/α6β1.
source: While Lu is capable of binding to Laminin-511/521 via Lama5, these laminins are also known as a ligand for Integrinα3β1/α6β1 (Kikkawa et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Lama5 may be secreted from biliary cell itself rather than the environmental niche cell.
source: Considering the accumulation of Lama5 in the vicinity of biliary cells, it is plausible that Lama5 may be secreted from biliary cell itself rather than the environmental niche cell.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of Lama5 accumulation around biliary cells.

claim: Lu may regulate the morphogenesis of DR via an Integrin-mediated manner.
source: Taking these evidences into account, Lu may regulate the morphogenesis of DR via an Integrin-mediated manner.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known interactions between Lu, Lama5, and integrins.

claim: Lu+ BC and Lu- BC are closely related, but distinct homogeneous populations.
source: By contrast, several stem cell markers such as CD24 and CD44 were expressed similarly between Lu+ BC and Lu- BC, suggesting that these cells are closely related, but distinct homogeneous populations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similar expression of stem cell markers between the two cell types.

claim: There is a causal link between Lu expression level and cell motility.
source: As expected, Lu+ BC showed significantly higher motility capacity than Lu- BC (Figure 3A), suggesting that there is a causal link between Lu expression level and cell motility.
evidence: This is an inference based on the scratch assay data.

claim: Lu may play a crucial role in the cell kinetics of biliary cell.
source: Thus, Lu+ BC and Lu- BC showed distinct features of cell motility and cyst formation in vitro. These results suggest that Lu may play a crucial role in the cell kinetics of biliary cell.
evidence: This is an inference based on the in vitro assay results.

claim: Lu expression is responsible for the characteristics of biliary cells.
source: These results strongly suggested that Lu- BC acquired the Lu+ BC-like phenotype after Lu expression, and that Lu might endow biliary cells with characteristics of spindle shape morphology and enhanced motility.
evidence: This is an inference based on the overexpression experiments.

claim: Lu plays a critical role in the definition of morphological heterogeneity of DR in vivo.
source: These results suggested that Lu plays a critical role in the definition of morphological heterogeneity of DR in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Bcam KO mouse experiments.

claim: Lu regulates the characteristic of DR by modulating the Itgb1 signaling.
source: These data strongly suggested that Lu regulates the characteristic of DR by modulating the Itgb1 signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the antibody experiments.

claim: The expression of Lu seemed to be downregulated in EpCAM+ cells at the tip of DR in the CDE model.
source: In line with the idea, intriguingly, the expression of Lu seemed to be downregulated in EpCAM+ cells at the tip of DR in the CDE model (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an observation from the study, supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The periportal region is rich in ECM including laminin whereas the parenchymal region is poor in it.
source: The discrepancy may be explained by the microenvironment surrounding LPCs; the periportal region is rich in ECM including laminin whereas the parenchymal region is poor in it.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about liver microenvironment.

claim: The loss of Lu in parenchymal area may be a sign of hepatocytic differentiation by the escape of LPC from laminin deposition.
source: Taking such microenvironment into consideration, the loss of Lu in parenchymal area may be a sign of hepatocytic differentiation by the escape of LPC from laminin deposition.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.
